question.problem:
Suppose we are given two vectors $a$ and $b$ where $a∦b.$ Find $s$ and $t,$ if 

$$
5a+4b=(2s+t)a+(s-t)b.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. So, the coefficients of $a$ must be equal, and the coefficients of $b$ must be equal.

Equating the coefficients, we get:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2s+t=5 \\ s-t=4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}3s & =9 \\ s & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting back into the first equation, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2s+t & =5 \\ 2(3)+t & =5 \\ 6+t & =5 \\ t & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that $s=3$ and $t=-1.$
